title: Rules and diagnostics
body: Rules are grouped like in Biome: syntax, schema, graph, text, markdown, style, trace, build, meta and custom. A code such as DOC301 is a public contract and never changes; retired codes are not reused. Messages are in English and every message has a hint. docc reports problems and changes nothing in the sources: there are no automatic fixes.

The preset recommended gives every rule a default level, and every rule is on by default. The rules style/hedging (DOC352) and style/timeless-words (DOC353) warn about vague and time-bound words. Word rules, the repeated-word rule and custom rules match text in Unicode NFC and skip text in backticks, so an identifier such as `new` is written in backticks.

Core rules are always errors and cannot be suppressed, switched off or given another level: broken JSON, duplicate keys, a missing title, invalid ids, the built-in schema, a missing kind schema (DOC109), duplicate ids, broken references, orphans, parent cycles, missing roots, links to hidden documents, bad includes, duplicate block anchors (DOC212), broken image paths (DOC213), bad code tags (DOC401), stale output (DOC501) and a stale `docc.lock` (DOC503).
Rule levels are set in [[config]]; the commands that run the rules are in [[commands]]; `docc.lock` is described in [[document-model#change_tracking]].
notable_rules: DOC209 graph/suspect-link warns when the target of a link changed after the link was confirmed in `docc.lock`: the source may no longer agree with it. Two or more links of one document to parts of the same target give one warning. DOC110 syntax/reserved-field-typo warns about a free field spelled almost like a reserved key (`parnet`, `hiden`). DOC202 names the nearest existing ids. DOC310 markdown/raw-html also reports links with a `javascript:`, `vbscript:` or `data:` address; docc does not rewrite them. DOC402 trace/code-changed warns when a `docc:begin` region changed: the document it points to may no longer agree with the code. DOC503 build/stale-lock is reported by `docc check` when `docc.lock` does not match the links.

DOC212 graph/duplicate-anchor reports a block anchor used twice in one document or equal to a heading anchor of its page. DOC213 graph/broken-file reports an image path that names no file in the sources, lies outside them or is not a png, jpg, jpeg, gif, svg or webp file. DOC214 graph/wrong-target-kind reports a reference whose target kind is not allowed by `x-docc-target`.

DOC314 style/manual-number warns when `numbering` is on and a title or a section key starts with its own number. DOC403 trace/uncovered warns when a document of a kind with `x-docc-covered` has no code tag. DOC303 also catches `N/A`, a lone dash, `see above` and `works correctly`, and their Russian forms.
diagnostic_format: Text form: file:line:column: level CODE (group/name) message, followed by a line with the hint, then a summary line such as checked 3 files: 1 error, 0 warnings. JSON form: an envelope with a summary (checked, errors, warnings, shown, truncated) and a diagnostics array of objects with code, rule, level, file, line, column, endLine, endColumn, message and hint. When the output is cut by max-diagnostics, truncated is true.
The order is deterministic: level, file path, line, column, code, rule name. Columns count Unicode characters of the source text, also inside strings with escape sequences.
see_also: Run `docc rules` for the list with current levels and `docc explain` with a code for a description and an example.
